title: Signal and Protocol
premise: Tamsin Marchetti, a xenolinguist whose mind has been reshaped by decades of contact with the beacon's alien signal, decodes a distress call in Vessic — a language extinct since the colony wars. The signal comes from a hidden ship carrying the last living Vessic speaker and proof that humanity's founding fleet committed genocide to claim the beacon. As the fleet's fragile truce expires, Tamsin must choose between loyalty to the institution that trained him and the truth that could end the war: broadcast the message, and both sides must reckon with a shared crime. He transmits it; the war collapses into uneasy reckoning rather than peace, and Tamsin, finally dreaming in Vessic, becomes the language's new keeper.
about_author: O. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years calibrating deep-space listening arrays before turning to fiction. They write about people who talk to machines for a living and live with what the machines say back.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On the derelict relay station Meridian, he performs his solitary maintenance ritual on a beacon whose commissioning records were purged generations ago. He notices his dreams have stopped using human words. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness masking pride in his strange vocation.

chapters.title: Grammar of Absence
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A routine diagnostic reveals the beacon has been transmitting an unscheduled pattern for eleven days — something he somehow failed to notice, which frightens him more than the anomaly itself. Emotional beat: creeping self-doubt about how much the signal has rewritten him.

chapters.title: Vessic
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He isolates the pattern and recognizes it from forbidden archive fragments: Vessic, declared extinct two centuries past after the colony wars. The message is structured as a distress call — and it knows his name. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Chain of Custody
chapters.summary: Fleet liaison Commander Idris Okonkwo's POV, arriving at Meridian under truce protocols. She claims the signal is a pirate spoof and orders the beacon sealed. Tamsin obeys but secretly copies the waveform. Emotional beat: institutional trust beginning to crack.

chapters.title: What the Archive Burned
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the station's quarantined records vault he finds evidence the beacon's original commissioning order was signed by the fleet itself — before the Vessic 'extinction.' Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing his whole career was built on a buried crime.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Fleet channels reveal the ceasefire expires in nineteen days, and hardliners on both sides are positioning. She suspects Tamsin has the full signal and begins surveilling him. Emotional beat: her own loyalty tested by orders she doesn't believe in.

chapters.title: The Ship That Shouldn't Be
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Following the distress vector, he finds a drifting vessel older than any registered hull, its crew long dead except one occupant in suspended animation: Sef Adari, last fluent speaker of Vessic. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by grief for everyone who died keeping this secret.

chapters.title: Waking Words
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sef wakes disoriented, speaking only Vessic; Tamsin discovers his altered mind can understand her when no translator can. Their first conversation is halting, intimate, and devastating — she learns her people are officially extinct. Emotional beat: two exiles finding a shared tongue.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. She explains the ship's cargo: the fleet's own logs proving the genocide, encoded in Vessic because the victors never bothered to learn the language they erased. The message was meant for the beacon all along. Emotional beat: rage and purpose fused.

chapters.title: Sealed Station
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Fleet command, tipped off, locks down Meridian and demands the 'spoof' source be surrendered. Okonkwo realizes the cover-up goes above her and quietly stalls the boarding party. Emotional beat: the moment obedience breaks.

chapters.title: Translation Is Betrayal
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Decoding the full message, he finds it names not just the perpetrators but the current fleets' founding families — including the lineage that funded his training. Every translation choice now carries political weight. Emotional beat: the weight of words as weapons.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Then Nine
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Skirmishes flare at the truce perimeter; the countdown accelerates as factions abandon protocol. She makes contact with Tamsin covertly, offering him a smuggler's route off-station — if he abandons the message. Emotional beat: temptation framed as rescue.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Vessic
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Sleepless, he finally dreams fully in Vessic and understands the beacon's original purpose: it was built as a confession machine, waiting two centuries for someone able to receive the truth. Emotional beat: acceptance of what he has become.

chapters.title: The Hardliner's Offer
chapters.summary: Fleet Admiral Ceylan's POV (antagonist). Ceylan offers Tamsin sanctuary, funding, and glory if he certifies the signal as fabricated. The offer includes erasure of Sef. Emotional beat: cold charm revealing the machinery of forgetting.

chapters.title: Refusal Protocol
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He declines, and Ceylan seizes the station. Sef is taken; Tamsin escapes into the beacon's maintenance shafts with the message core. Emotional beat: fear transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Choice
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Ordered to hunt Tamsin, she instead feeds him the fleet's authentication codes — committing treason to let one true message through. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the price of her career and possibly her life.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. With hours before the truce expires, he overrides the beacon and transmits the Vessic confession on every open channel, narrating it aloud in both languages so no filter can suppress it. Emotional beat: terror and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Ceylan's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Ceylan's POV. The admiral attempts to jam the transmission and declare Tamsin a saboteur, but the message is already propagating through civilian relays; mutiny spreads through her own crews. Emotional beat: power unraveling faster than it can lie.

chapters.title: The Truce Expires
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Fleets hold fire as the confession floods every screen; soldiers on both sides refuse the order to engage. Sef, freed by sympathetic crew, speaks Vessic over open comms — a dead language alive again in ten thousand ears. Emotional beat: catharsis held on a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Reckoning, Not Peace
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Armistice talks begin under new terms, ugly and honest. Ceylan is arrested by her own officers. Okonkwo surrenders herself for treason, expecting trial. Emotional beat: justice without comfort.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The beacon's original mission complete, he chooses to stay — retraining a new generation of listeners, teaching Vessic alongside Sef. His dreams no longer feel like loss. Emotional beat: quiet belonging found in the aftermath.

chapters.title: Signal and Protocol
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, closing frame. Years later, she records the first entry of a restored Vessic archive and sends it to the beacon, where Tamsin answers in kind. The war is remembered honestly now — because someone kept the signal and broke the protocol. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled, memory made durable.
